newsitem.title: UK: North Sea crudes find buyers but Brent neglected.
newsitem.headline: North Sea crudes find buyers but Brent neglected.

text.p: North Sea gas oil-rich crudes found no shortage of buyers as refiners collected what little was left of October loading Oseberg and other distillate grades at the expense of benchmark Brent, dealers said.
The prompt 15-day spread was slightly weaker in the afternoon, talking some two cents down at +47/+49 cents for Nov/Dec. Dec/Jan traded at +60 cents.
Brent CFDs also weakened with next week's dates being talked at Nov -2/-1, down from Nov +1/+3 cents earlier in the day.
An Oct 16-18 cargo traded between refiners at Nov evens but traders expected weaker numbers for later deals.
One of the two Brent dates in Wednesday's paper chains was kept early by an equity holder.

Oseberg was the best performing North Sea crude with differentials to match. The grade, which has a high gas oil yield, traded at Dated Brent +41/+42/+43 cents for cargoes loading in the third decade.
One million barrels of Flotta were heard done with late pricing taking the North Sea sour grade to an equivalent Dated Brent -56 cents, which one broker said was an unlikely number.
The West African market was quiet though Nigerian Bonny Light was talked at consistently higher numbers.
One dealer questioned the reported trade of a Bonny Light cargo at Dated Brent +60 cents for a VLCC load CIF NWE, which he said was offloaded in three different locations en route to Rotterdam.
Another October cargo traded at Dated +57 cents to a Spanish refiner on Tuesday.
"We're just waiting for the first November nominations, then it is onwards and upwards," a trader said.
Urals was also strong, despite a heavy loading schedule from Novorossiisk, dealers said.
